proposal.description_long: UK Parliament’s historic Hansard profile records Robert Maxwell as representing Buckingham from October 15, 1964, through June 18, 1970. The Parliament-hosted results for the 1964 general election identify the winning Labour candidate as Ian Robert Maxwell and record 23,085 votes; the Conservative candidate received 21,604 and the Liberal candidate 5,578. These official records support the election date, constituency, party, and end of Maxwell’s parliamentary service. They do not support the linked TrumpFile page’s assertions about intelligence ties, and those allegations are not needed to describe the election. The event occurred decades before Donald Trump’s political career and the supplied sources identify no connection between Trump and Maxwell’s election. The existing title’s “Trump:” prefix therefore implies a relationship the evidence does not show. This draft supplies a concise, verifiable historical description and recommends excluding the item from a Trump-specific chronology unless an independently sourced connection is established. It does not repeat unsupported intelligence claims or convert the election entry into a biography.
proposal.description_medium: The UK Parliament’s historic Hansard profile records Robert Maxwell as representing Buckingham from October 15, 1964, to June 18, 1970. The History of Parliament database identifies him as a Labour member elected in the 1964 general election. These records establish the election and service dates; they do not establish the intelligence allegations in the linked timeline or a connection to Donald Trump.
